{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "She stood. Her knees had gone stiff from the floor, and she felt the stiffness the way she felt everything now, as if from a small distance.

"You ate my bread," she said. "The end pieces. I thought it was mice."

"Only when there was enough."

"There was never enough."

He accepted that. He did not apologize, and she found she was grateful; an apology would have made him a stranger again, someone who owed her something, and she was tired of being owed.

The lamp below guttered and steadied. Through the knothole its light came up in a thread and lay across the toe of his boot. She saw that the boot had been mended with fishing line, small even stitches, the work of someone with a great deal of time.

"My father knew," she said. It was not a question.

"He brought the ladder up. The first night." He paused. "He said the house was too large for one woman and one grief, and that a house should be full of what it could hold."

Ines laughed, once, and the sound surprised them both. It was her father's sentence exactly. She could hear him saying it, the way he weighted the word hold.

"Come down," she said.

He did not move.

"I'm not afraid," she said. "You made sure of that. So come down and eat at a table, and tell me your name, and stop listening to me through the floor."

After a moment he stepped over the threshold, and the board did not complain at all."}
